questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

She blew the candles on the cake.

options.text: The candles on the cake were blew by her.
The candles on the cake were blown by her.
The candles on the cake were being blown by her.
The candles on the cake is blown by her.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'The candles on the cake were blown by her.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Past Tense and in Active Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a sentence in Past Tense from Active voice to Passive voice:
 
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence become the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The helping verb comes before the object in the passive voice as the passive voice starts with the object of the active voice.
 
• Convert the verb into past participle or 3rd form of the verb.
 
• Structure: Subject + V2 + object (Active Voice)__
 
 

 Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject __(Passive Voice)__ 

__
 
• Solution: *She blew the candles on the cake. *(Active Voice)

 * The candles on the cake were blown by her. *(Passive Voice)

 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 'The candles on the cake were blown by her.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, the sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
 
• Example: *He reads a novel. *(Active Voice)

 * A novel is read by him. *(Passive Voice)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

She paid a high price for the clothes she __brought at__ the boutique.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bought at**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the above sentence there should be **bought **instead of **brought**.
 
• The word **Bought **is the past tense and past participle of the verb to purchase, which implies “to get something by paying cash for it.
 
• *Example *: I **bought **this ring for you.
 
• The word **Brought **is the past tense and past participle of the verb to bring, which suggests “to carry somebody or something to a place or individual.
 
• *Example *: I** brought** you something to eat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Tenses Chart

 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
Tenses

 
 
 
Rules and Formula

 
 
 

 
 
Simple Present Tense

 
 
 
Subject + Verb in the base form/third person plural form + the rest of the sentence

 
 
 

 
 
Present Continuous Tense

 
 
 
Subject + Helping Verb(am/is/are) + Main verb + ing + the rest of the sentence 

 
 
 

 
 
Present Perfect Tense

 
 
 
Subject + Helping Verb (have/has) + Past participle of the main verb + the rest of the sentence along with the time frame

 
 
 

 
 
Present Perfect Continuous Tense

 
 
 
Subject + Have/Has + Been + Verb+ ing + the rest of the sentence

 
 
 

 
 
Simple Past Tense

 
 
 
Subject + Verb + ed / verb in the past tense + the rest of the sentence

 
 
 

 
 
Past Continuous Tense 

 
 
 
Subject + Helping Verb(was/were) + Main verb + ing + the rest of the sentence

 
 
 

 
 
Past Perfect Tense

 
 
 
Subject + Helping Verb (had) + Past participle of the main verb + the rest of the sentence along with the time frame.

 
 
 

 
 
Past Perfect Continuous Tense

 
 
 
Subject + Had + Been + Verb + ing + the rest of the sentence

 
 
 

 
 
Simple Future Tense

 
 
 
Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object

 
 
 

 
 
Future Continuous Tense

 
 
 
Subject + will be/shall be + V1 + ing + Object

 
 
 

 
 
Future Perfect Tense

 
 
 
Subject + will have/shall have + V3 + Object

 
 
 

 
 
Future Perfect Continuous Tense

 
 
 
Subject + will have been + V1 + ing + Object

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The discovery of treasure under the Bermuda Triangle is probably a __hoax__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **"Trick"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given options, **"Trick"** is the most appropriate synonym of **"hoax"**.
 
• **Hoax:** a trick/ method of deception intended to fool others.
 
 
• **Example:** People were **hoaxed** by the fake matrimonial website.
 
 
 
• Thus, ***option 4) ***is the correct alternative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let us understand the meaning of other options as well.

__
 
• **Analogy: **a comparison of two, otherwise unrelated, things based on similarities in one specific area.
 
• **Bonanza:** something that generates tremendous opportunities or large earnings all of a sudden
 
• **Delusion: **something that is false or unreal but is perceived to be true or real.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• **Trick**: A trick refers to a cunning or deceitful action intended to deceive or manipulate someone. It involves using clever tactics or strategies to achieve a desired outcome. In the context of the sentence, "hoax" implies a deliberate deception, making "trick" a suitable synonym.
 
• **Delusion**: A delusion, on the other hand, refers to a persistent false belief or perception that is firmly held despite evidence to the contrary. It often involves a distorted view of reality and can be associated with mental health conditions such as schizophrenia or delusional disorder. While a hoax can create a temporary delusion, the focus is more on the act of deception rather than the enduring false belief itself.
 
• **Considering the context of the sentence you provided, "trick" is indeed a more appropriate synonym for "hoax."**
